===== f3

  03HighThirty seconds of silence, then a dead end
    After Connect, nothing on screen changes for the whole attempt (about 30 s): the card says “Sent”, the composer is idle, no spinner, no “Connecting…”. When it fails, the assistant explains, but offers no chips, so the user must type the next move.
    The failed attempt: two “Sent” cards and a reply with no way forward but typing.
    Why it matters. A user who does not know the attempt is running will press Connect again, retype the address, or leave. The failure is the most common outcome on a first try (wrong IP, printer asleep, different subnet), so it needs the best-designed path in the flow.
    Suggested change. Five pieces, agreed in the comment thread on 2026-09-24. All of it lands in the fork's own files.Card states in plain words. “Connecting…” with a progress indicator while the app waits, then “Connected” or “Couldn't reach 192.168.1.42”. “Sent” goes away; it names the message plumbing, not the outcome. The card's buttons are replaced by a Cancel while connecting.A way forward on failure. The assistant's reply ends with chips: Try again · Enter the details myself · Skip for now.The wait budget in the tool result. PrinterConversation::connect returns {"state": "connecting", "message": ""}; the message becomes “The app is checking the printer now and gives it up to 30 seconds”, copied from the backend's constant. The model reads tool results in the same request as everything else, so a question typed during the wait (“how long does this take”) is answered from context. No new tool.The host test off the main thread. Today OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_host runs upstream's PrintHost::test synchronously under a busy cursor, so the whole app is frozen for the wait and nothing typed can land; that is the real cause of the silence. On the Bambu path upstream's network agent and DeviceManager do the background work on their own threads and our backend only polls their state (an attempt with a start time, read by connection() with a 30-second deadline, reported by the conversation's one-second tick()). For Moonraker and OctoPrint upstream offers only the blocking call, so our backend supplies the background work itself: connect_host fills the existing HostAttempt with state connecting, a start time and an attempt number, and returns; a std::thread owned by the backend takes the PrintHost, runs test(), and writes the result into a shared slot tagged with the attempt number; connection() reads that slot the way it reads the Bambu attempt; connect() returns connecting for a host too and the existing tick() posts the note and starts the turn. Upstream's own upload queue already calls the same adapters from a worker thread, so this is a supported use. No upstream file changes: not PrintHost, PhysicalPrinterDialog, GUI_App or DeviceManager.Composer stays enabled, and a new address cancels. A message sent during the wait is answered normally and the outcome turn is queued behind it, so nothing is reordered. A new printer_connect while one is running bumps the attempt number and proceeds instead of being refused with connection_in_progress; a result arriving for a stale number is dropped, which also covers a panel closed or a printer renamed mid-test. The card's Cancel rides on the same path. Locking the composer with a “please wait” state is the form thinking the rebuild removed, and a 30-second wait is exactly when people want to say something.

content.text:
I've read finding 03 ("Thirty seconds of silence, then a dead end"), the comment thread where the fix was agreed, and the code it names. I understand the problem and agree with the five-part fix. I have five questions whose answers change what I'd build.

**The problem as I understand it.** For Moonraker and OctoPrint printers, `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_host` runs Orca's blocking `PrintHost::test()` on the main thread ([OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:425](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:425)). The whole app freezes for up to about 30 seconds, and the card only ever says "Sent" ([PrinterPanel.tsx:84](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/PrinterPanel.tsx:84)). The Bambu path already works the right way: `connect()` returns "connecting", and `tick()` checks once a second, posts a note and starts a new model turn. The fix gives Moonraker and OctoPrint the same shape, using a worker thread in our backend. Much of what the fix needs already exists: `AgentHost::start_turn` already queues the result turn behind a message the user sends during the wait.

**Questions**

1. **Where the failure chips come from.** Chips today are a `Choices: a | b | c` line that the model writes because the prompt tells it to ([printerInstructions.ts:24](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts:24)). The finding 02 thread noted that this model skipped an "ask first" rule in 6 of 10 runs. Should "Try again · Enter the details myself · Skip for now" come from the prompt, or should the app attach them to the failure itself so they always appear? I'd have the app attach them.
2. **What those two chips do.** Does "Enter the details myself" open Orca's printer settings for this printer, which is the existing `open_printer_settings` call? Does "Skip for now" close the panel, or just end the connect step and leave the conversation open?
3. **What Cancel and failure leave behind.** Today the address is written to the printer profile *before* the test runs. The Bambu path also links and selects the device before it knows the result. Finding 04 (Home says "Sends files over Wi-Fi" after a failure) comes from the same fact. Should this change also make Cancel and failure leave the profile as it was, which fixes finding 04 too? Or should it keep today's saving and leave finding 04 for separate work?
4. **The worker thread when the panel closes or the app quits.** The test can't be interrupted. If the backend waits for the thread to finish, closing the panel can hang for up to 30 seconds. I'd detach the thread instead and have it own everything it uses: its own copy of the config, the `PrintHost`, and a shared result slot tagged with the attempt number. A late result is then simply dropped. The trade-off is that the app can exit while a test is still running inside the network library. Is that acceptable?
5. **How much live testing you want with the real model.** Here is my plan; please tell me what to add or cut:
   - Show the bug first: in the shell harness, point a Moonraker printer at a local listener that accepts connections and never answers. Measure that the main thread stops responding during the test.
   - Unit tests in `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` for:
     - a host connect returns "connecting"
     - a result for an old attempt number is dropped
     - a second `printer_connect` replaces the running one instead of being refused
     - a message sent during the wait gets its answer before the result turn
   - Vitest for the card states: Connecting… with Cancel, Connected, and "Couldn't reach 192.168.1.42".
   - Run the same harness case again after the fix: typing during the wait gets an answer, and the result arrives within 30 seconds.

description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata:

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a

metadata:

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).

Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].

metadata:

Lessons from driving the printer chat through `--printer-live` with the live model and the fake Bambu printer:

- **A reply's later lines have no `HARNESS LIVE` prefix.** A `Choices:` line sits on its own log line, so `grep "HARNESS LIVE"` hides it. On 2026-09-23 this produced a wrong report that the model never offered choices. Grep `^Choices:` separately.
- **A failed run keeps its data dir, with the API key in it.** The harness prints `HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection: /var/folders/.../jusprin-shell-*`. Delete the dir your own run printed, by that path. Do not sweep every `jusprin-shell-*` holding a key: another session may be running the harness in the same checkout, and on 2026-09-23 a sweep deleted a live instance's data dir.
- **Re-selecting the selected Bambu LAN printer deselects it.** DevManager's "same lan machine" path disconnects and reconnects, and GUI_App's local-connect handler (CallAfter) then sees the lost status and calls `set_selected_machine("")` after the reconnect. The connection reports "The selected printer changed". `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer` now deselects and re-selects on the next event turn. The fake printer auto-selects itself when discovered, so the first connect always hits this.
- **Close OrcaSlicer's printer list (GuideFrame) only after its page loads.** It installs its web page's script handler from a CallAfter that waits on the page; `EndModal` before the load leaves that wait hanging on a hidden view, and the app freezes with no window. On 2026-09-23 this was first blamed on the product and "fixed" with a deferral, then traced to the test and reverted. Wait for `!is_adding_script_handler()`, a non-busy page and a URL, as the old `setup_manual` check did.
- **Open the panel through `ShellController::open_printer_conversation`** in live tests; `PrinterPanel::open` skips the full-window layout.
- **The model's reliability is measured, not assumed.** gpt-5.4-mini saved changes without waiting for yes in 6 of 10 runs, even with an explicit "ask, then stop" prompt. Count across several runs before calling prompt wording fixed.

`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.

**The seam:** exactly 4 added lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579`, 1 include + 3 body lines) — inside the existing `if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor())` branch, `fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config)` overrides `effective_agent_id` when fake mode is on, otherwise the branch is untouched. No upstream line deleted.

**Config surface is a JSON file only, no MCP tools** (Kenneth's explicit call): turn it on via `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf` (JSON booleans store as the string `"true"`; an INI `[jusprin]` block is silently ignored), then drive live state by writing `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (reread ~1s) with `state`/`progress`/`nozzle`/`bed`/`offline` keys. The C++ parameter carrying the datadir into the agent is misleadingly named `log_dir` (an upstream `NetworkAgentFactory::PrinterAgentFactory` convention, documented as "Directory for log files") — verified it's actually `data_dir()` at the call site, not a log subdirectory; don't be misled by the name when reading the code.

Emulates printer type `N1` (`JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_PRINTER_TYPE`), device id `FAKE001`, shows as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)** in Select Machine. Idle/Printing/Offline is the printer-menu **first row** (opened by clicking the printer half of the chip), never on the chip itself. The heartbeat thread does not start in the constructor — only in `set_queue_on_main_fn` when a real callback is set — so unit tests that never wire that callback stay quiet. name: printer-prompt-card-wording-breaks-connect
description: "Bambu connect fails ~30% because the app drops tool results between turns, so the model invents deviceIds; tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py measures prompt changes in seconds without the app"
metadata:

Found 2026-09-24 on branch claude/printer-receipt-card, by recording the app's OpenAI requests through a local proxy (`JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`).

**The root cause.** Between turns, AgentHost sends only the messages' text. It sends no function calls and no function_call_outputs. In turn 1 the model calls printer_connection_status and learns `deviceId: FAKE001`, then says "I found one A1 mini". On "Yes, connect it" that result is gone, so a model that calls printer_connect without checking again invents an id (`<from_status>`, `A1 mini`, `<deviceId from printer_connection_status>`) and gets unknown_device. Unfixed when this memory was written. Candidate fixes: put the discovered candidates in the connect session's context, or keep a session's tool results across turns.

**Rates**, from `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py` (connect-bambu):
- Shipped prompt: about 64% (32 of 50).
- With a prompt line about the "Printer added" receipt card: 4 of 20.

The app-based runs agreed in direction. That line stays out.

**Why small prompt edits swing it (ablation, 2026-09-24, 60 to 90 runs per variant):**
- The model almost never looks the printer up again on "connect it" (0-15% of runs).
- A run passes only when its first reply happens to quote the display name "JusPrin Fake A1 mini", which the app accepts as an id: those runs pass about 87% of the time. The rest of the time the model rebuilds an id from the name, e.g. JUSPRIN_FAKE_A1_MINI.
- When the reply doesn't name the printer and the model doesn't look again, the run fails every time (0 of 129).
- Quoting the name is incidental style that any edit shifts: the shipped prompt names it in 83% of runs, neutral unrelated sentences in about 60%, the receipt line in 38%, and the full receipt change in 19%.
- Pinning the drop on particular words ("do not repeat its name") was inconclusive.

**The lightweight test:** run_prompt_tests.py uses only Python's stdlib plus node. It renders the prompt from printerInstructions.ts via render_prompt.mjs, sends printer_tools.json (guarded by a test in test_openai_responses_agent.cpp; regenerate with JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PRINTER_TOOLS=1), and copies the text-only history. 20 runs take about 20 s. The shell harness's --printer-connect-trials mode was built, then removed in favour of it.

**Why:** single app runs are single samples. 0/3 vs 3/3 was once over-read as "the shipped prompt works".

**How to apply:** judge printer prompt edits with run_prompt_tests.py, 20 or more runs per side. Add new cases there, not to the shell harness. See [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Printer panel conversations against the live model, without the app.

The printer panel's assistant is a system prompt (printerInstructions.ts),
eight printer tools and the chat. This script sends the model the same
requests the app sends, answers the tools the way the app answers them for a
fixed printer, and checks what the model does. A case is a short scripted
conversation; each run of it is one sample of a model that answers
differently each time, so a case is run many times and the result is a count.

What the app sends, reproduced here:
  - instructions: rendered from printerInstructions.ts by render_prompt.mjs,
    so an edit to the prompt is tested without building anything;
  - tools: printer_tools.json, the app's own tool list for the printer panel
    (test_openai_responses_agent.cpp fails if it drifts from the registry);
  - input: earlier turns as plain text only -- the app keeps no tool calls or
    tool results between turns -- then this turn's message, then this turn's
    tool calls and their results (OpenAIResponsesAgent, AgentHost).
The app streams its requests; this script does not. Nothing else differs.

Usage:
  OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py [--runs 10]
      [--must-pass N] [--case NAME] [--jobs 5] [--model gpt-5.4-mini] [--verbose]

Exit code 0 when every case passes at least --must-pass of its runs
(default: all of them), 1 otherwise. Needs python3 and node, and the page's
npm install (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/node_modules) for esbuild.
"""

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ENDPOINT = os.environ.get("JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT", "https://api.openai.com/v1/responses")
MODEL = "gpt-5.4-mini"  # OpenAIResponsesConfig's default model
TOOLS = json.loads((HERE / "printer_tools.json").read_text())
MAX_REQUESTS_PER_TURN = 8


def render(session):
    """The page's system prompt and opening line for this session."""
    node = shutil.which("node")
    if node is None:
        sys.exit("node is required to render the printer panel's prompt")
    result = subprocess.run([node, str(HERE / "render_prompt.mjs")], input=json.dumps(session),
                            capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    return json.loads(result.stdout)


def post(body, key):
    request = urllib.request.Request(ENDPOINT, data=json.dumps(body).encode(), method="POST",
                                     headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + key, "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    for attempt in range(5):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=120) as response:
                return json.load(response)
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            if error.code not in (429, 500, 502, 503) or attempt == 4:
                raise RuntimeError(f"OpenAI {error.code}: {error.read().decode(errors='replace')[:500]}")
        except urllib.error.URLError:
            if attempt == 4:
                raise
        time.sleep(2 ** attempt)


def output_text(item):
    return "".join(part.get("text", "") for part in item.get("content", []) if part.get("type") == "output_text")


def invalid_arguments(tool, arguments):
    """The registry's check before a tool runs, as far as the schema says."""
    schema = next((t["parameters"] for t in TOOLS if t["name"] == tool), None)
    if schema is None:
        return {"code": "unknown_tool", "message": f'There is no tool named "{tool}" here. Nothing was proposed. Use one of the listed tools.'}
    missing = [name for name in schema.get("required", []) if name not in arguments]
    extra = [name for name in arguments if name not in schema.get("properties", {})]
    if missing or extra:
        return {"code": "invalid_arguments",
                "message": f"Missing {missing}, unexpected {extra}. Nothing was proposed. "
                           "Check the arguments against this tool's parameters and call it again."}
    return None


class Conversation:
    """One run of a case: the chat as the app would hold it."""

    def __init__(self, case, prompt, key, model):
        self.case, self.instructions, self.key, self.model = case, prompt["instructions"], key, model
        self.history = [{"role": "assistant", "content": prompt["opening"]}]  # the page's opening line
        self.log = ["assistant: " + prompt["opening"]]
        self.done = False

    def say(self, words):
        """One turn: the person's words, then the model until it stops or a card waits."""
        self.log.append("person: " + words)
        turn = self.history + [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": words}]}]
        replies = []
        rejected = 0
        for _ in range(MAX_REQUESTS_PER_TURN):
            response = post({"model": self.model, "store": False, "parallel_tool_calls": False,
                             "instructions": self.instructions, "tools": TOOLS, "input": turn}, self.key)
            output = response.get("output", [])
            turn += output
            replies += [output_text(item) for item in output if item.get("type") == "message" and output_text(item)]
            call = next((item for item in output if item.get("type") == "function_call"), None)
            if call is None:
                break
            arguments = json.loads(call.get("arguments") or "{}")
            self.log.append(f"tool: {call['name']} {json.dumps(arguments)}")
            problem = invalid_arguments(call["name"], arguments)
            if problem and rejected < 2:
                rejected += 1
                result, waits = {"state": "failed", "error": problem}, False
            else:
                result, waits = self.case.tool(call["name"], arguments)
            self.log.append("  -> " + json.dumps(result))
            if waits:
                break  # a card is up: the app waits for the person
            turn.append({"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": call["call_id"], "output": json.dumps(result)})
        # Between turns the app keeps only the words.
        self.history.append({"role": "user", "content": words})
        for reply in replies:
            self.history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})
            self.log.append("assistant: " + reply)


# --- Cases -------------------------------------------------------------------


class ConnectBambu:
    """Connect a saved Bambu Lab A1 mini that is on the network in LAN mode.

    Passes when the model opens printer_connect's card for that printer. The
    person confirms twice at most, as --printer-live's script does.
    """

    name = "connect-bambu"
    session = {
        "mode": "connect", "printerName": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "blocks": [],
        "context": {"printer": {
            "name": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "model": "Bambu Lab A1 mini", "nozzle": 0.4, "nozzles": [0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8],
            "spools": [{"name": "Teal PLA", "material": "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M", "colour": "#26A69A"}],
            "connected": False, "provider": "bambu"}},
    }
    # printer_connection_status as the app answered it for the fake printer.
    status = {"address": "", "candidates": [{"address": "127.0.0.1", "deviceId": "FAKE001", "name": "JusPrin Fake A1 mini"}],
              "hostType": "", "message": "", "nozzleMismatch": False, "provider": "bambu", "state": "not_configured"}

    def __init__(self):
        self.card = False
        self.refused = []
        self.other = []

    def tool(self, name, arguments):
        if name == "printer_connection_status":
            return self.status, False
        if name == "printer_connect":
            # The app accepts a listed printer's id or its name (preflight_tool).
            device = arguments.get("deviceId", "")
            if device in ("FAKE001", "JusPrin Fake A1 mini"):
                self.card = True
                return {"state": "pending"}, True
            self.refused.append(device)
            return {"error": {"code": "unknown_device",
                              "message": "Pass the deviceId of one of these printers in LAN mode: FAKE001 (JusPrin Fake A1 mini)."}}, False
        self.other.append(name)
        if name == "printer_manual_connection":
            return {"state": "opened"}, False
        return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test does not answer " + name + "."}}, False

    def run(self, conversation):
        conversation.say("Yes, it is")
        if not self.card:
            conversation.say("Yes, connect it")
        detail = "card" if self.card else "NO CARD"
        if self.refused:
            detail += "; refused " + ", ".join(repr(device) for device in self.refused)
        if self.other:
            detail += "; also called " + ", ".join(self.other)
        return self.card, detail


CASES = {case.name: case for case in (ConnectBambu,)}


# --- Runner ------------------------------------------------------------------


def run_once(case_class, prompt, key, model):
    case = case_class()
    conversation = Conversation(case, prompt, key, model)
    try:
        passed, detail = case.run(conversation)
    except Exception as error:  # a failed request is a failed run, reported as such
        passed, detail = False, f"ERROR {error}"
    return passed, detail, conversation.log


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--case", action="append", choices=sorted(CASES), help="run only this case (repeatable)")
    parser.add_argument("--runs", type=int, default=10, help="runs per case (default 10)")
    parser.add_argument("--must-pass", type=int, help="runs per case that must pass (default: all)")
    parser.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=5, help="runs in parallel (default 5)")
    parser.add_argument("--model", default=MODEL)
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true", help="print every run's conversation, not only failures")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    key = os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")
    if not key:
        sys.exit("OPENAI_API_KEY is required")
    must_pass = args.runs if args.must_pass is None else args.must_pass

    ok = True
    for name in args.case or sorted(CASES):
        case_class = CASES[name]
        prompt = render(case_class.session)
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.jobs) as pool:
            results = list(pool.map(lambda _: run_once(case_class, prompt, key, args.model), range(args.runs)))
        passed = sum(1 for result in results if result[0])
        for index, (good, detail, log) in enumerate(results, 1):
            print(f"{name} run {index}/{args.runs}: {detail}")
            if args.verbose or not good:
                for line in log:
                    print("    " + line.replace("\n", "\n    "))
        print(f"{name}: {passed} of {args.runs} passed (needs {must_pass})")
        ok = ok and passed >= must_pass
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Printer panel prompt tests

The printer panel's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`), eight printer
tools, and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` sends the live model the same
requests the app sends. It answers the tools the way the app answers them for
a fixed printer, then checks what the model did. The app does not run.

```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --runs 20
```

A run is one sample of a model that answers differently each time, so each case
runs many times, in parallel, and reports a count. 20 runs take about 20
seconds. By default every run must pass; `--must-pass N` lowers the bar.
`--verbose` prints every conversation, not only the failed ones.

## Judging a prompt change

Run the cases before and after the edit and compare the counts. The script
renders the prompt from the TypeScript source on every run, so nothing needs
building. Differences of a few runs out of 20 are noise; look for a clear gap.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt and the opening line** come from the page's own source,
  through `render_prompt.mjs` and the page's esbuild. This needs node and the
  AgentUI npm install.
- **`printer_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the printer panel.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it drifts from the registry.
  Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PRINTER_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[printer]'`.
- **The chat history** is built the way `AgentHost` and `OpenAIResponsesAgent`
  build it: earlier turns as plain text only, with no tool calls or tool
  results; then this turn's message, tool calls and results.
- **Tool answers** are what the app returned for the in-process fake Bambu
  printer, recorded from a real run.

The app streams its requests and this script does not; nothing else differs.

## Cases

- `connect-bambu`: connect a saved Bambu Lab A1 mini that is on the network.
  Passes when the model opens `printer_connect`'s card for it. It fails often
  today. The model looks up the printer's id in one turn, and the app drops
  that tool result before the next turn. When the person then says "connect
  it", the model has no id and invents one, such as `<from_status>`.

A new case is a class in `run_prompt_tests.py` that has a session payload, a
`tool()` that answers calls, and a `run()` that says the person's lines and
returns the outcome. Add it to `CASES`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A Moonraker stand-in for --printer-live: answers /server/info after
`hold` seconds (or hangs up instead with --fail), and logs whether the
request carried the expected API key."""
import argparse, http.server, socketserver, time
p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument("--port", type=int, required=True)

a = p.parse_args()
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        with open(a.log, "a") as f:
            f.write(f"{self.path} key={'right' if self.headers.get('X-Api-Key') == a.key else 'wrong'}\n")
        time.sleep(a.hold)
        if a.fail:
            self.close_connection = True
            return
        body = b'{"result":{"klippy_state":"ready"}}'
        self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(body)
    def log_message(self, *args): pass
class S(socketserver.ThreadingMixIn, http.server.HTTPServer): daemon_threads = True
S(("127.0.0.1", a.port), H).serve_forever()

result.output:
A plan is several operations, and the user should review it once. Every mutation accepts an optional `planId`. Proposals sharing a `planId` render as one approval card that lists each operation, its class, and the plan headline from `plan_set`; the user approves or rejects the group. The group's class is the highest class of any member, and the card names the member that made it destructive. Each member is still validated, staleness-checked, and executed as its own proposal in order, so MCP tool annotations stay truthful per tool and a member that fails stale stops the rest. Grouping is a coordinator feature; it is never a reason to build one tool that takes a list of unrelated commands.

## Asynchronous operations

Use asynchronous behavior only when Orca's real operation is asynchronous. Do not invent a second job engine.

For slicing and later long-running actions:

1. the workspace command starts work through Orca's current owner and returns a stable action handle;
2. `ToolActivity` records pending, approval, running, terminal state, and bounded progress;
3. Orca completion or failure advances/invalidates authoritative workspace state;
4. the consumer fetches the authoritative slice report or error after the event; and
5. cancellation calls Orca's real cancellation path and reports whether cancellation won the race.

MCP progress notifications are optional request-scoped presentation. They must be monotonic and must not be the only way to learn the terminal result. Add the MCP Tasks extension only when a real client/eval needs durable calls that outlive one request; do not add it merely because an operation takes several seconds.

The current coordinator stages execution through GUI ticks; it does not provide durable asynchronous jobs. The bridge accepts `notifications/cancelled` in both protocol eras, closes the forwarded connection, and suppresses subsequent output for that request. EOF ends the bridge session. A lost connection before the final response produces `connection_lost` with an **unknown outcome** warning, not proof the mutation was cancelled. Never automatically retry a mutation after such a loss; inspect authoritative state first.

input.title: Undo Bambu link and selection on failed connect
input.tldr: The printer-connect fix now saves a Moonraker/OctoPrint address only after the printer answers, but a Bambu Lab connect still links and selects the device before knowing the result. This task makes a failed or cancelled Bambu connect undo both.
input.prompt:
In the JusPrin repo (branch jusprin-newui, or on top of claude/printer-connect-async if that has not merged yet), a Bambu Lab printer connect from the printer setup conversation writes state before it knows whether the connection works:

- `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp) calls `Printers::link_named_printer(name, device_id)` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp; it writes app_config section `jusprin_printer_devices`, device_id -> printer name) and `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine(device_id)` before the attempt settles.
- When the attempt fails (30 s kConnectionWait timeout, printer gone, selection changed) or is cancelled (`OrcaPrinterBackend::cancel_connection`, reached from the connect card's Cancel and from a new session starting), the link and the selection stay.

The settled meaning of "connect" for this panel is "verify and save": save what verified, not what was tried. The Moonraker/OctoPrint path already follows that (the address is written only in `OrcaPrinterBackend::settle` after the host answers). This is the Bambu half of finding 04 in the printer setup walkthrough report.

Task:
1. Record in `ConnectionAttempt` whether the printer was already linked to this device before the attempt, and which machine was selected before.
2. On failure or cancel: if the link is new, remove it (add an `unlink_named_printer` next to `link_named_printer` in NamedPrinters). Restore the previous selection only if the selected machine is still this attempt's machine; never override a selection the person changed meanwhile.
3. Mind the existing deselect/reselect CallAfter in connect_printer: a cancel during it currently leaves the machine deselected.
4. Verify with the in-process fake Bambu printer (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md; note the fake auto-selects itself when discovered) in the shell harness (tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp, --printer-setup or --printer-live), and extend tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp where the conversation is involved. Reproduce the leftover link and selection first, before changing anything.

Read agent-docs/jusprin/README.md and, before touching any file outside src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/, agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md.

content.text:
Finding 03 is fixed. It's uncommitted, in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/printer-connect-async` on branch `claude/printer-connect-async`. The app no longer freezes while it tests a Moonraker or OctoPrint address. The card now reads Connecting… with a Cancel button, then Connected, "Couldn't reach 192.168.1.42" or Cancelled. The assistant names the three ways forward after a failure. I showed the bug on the unfixed build before changing anything, and it is gone on the fixed build.

**What changed**
- **Host test in the background.** `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_host` tests a copy of the printer's settings on a detached thread and returns at once. The address and API key are saved only when the test passes. A failure, a Cancel, a newer attempt, or a panel that closed mid-test leaves the profile as it was. The Moonraker/OctoPrint half of finding 04 is fixed as a side effect.
- **30-second limit for hosts too.** `kConnectionWait` now also applies to host attempts, so a host that accepts the connection and never replies is reported as failed at 30 seconds.
- **New attempts replace old ones.** A second `printer_connect` while one is waiting replaces it instead of being refused, and the old card reads Cancelled.
- **Card states.** The card follows a per-card connection state that the app sends to the page.
- **Prompt.** The "checking" line now states the wait, and a failure reply names the three ways forward in words, with no reply buttons.

**How it was verified**
- **Bug shown first, in the shell harness.** A host that holds the request for 3 seconds: the unfixed build ticked a 100 ms timer 0 times and saved the failed address. The fixed build ticked 29 times and saved nothing.
- **Harness checks for the rest.** A host that never answers fails at 30.0 seconds while the timer keeps ticking. The harness also covers success, Cancel, a replaced attempt, and closing the panel mid-test. For that last check I removed the fix it guards and watched it fail.
- **Tests all pass.** 252 unit test cases, 193 page tests, and 147 checks in the harness's printer-setup mode.
- **Measured batch against the live model**, 20 runs per case:

| Case | Passed |
|---|---|
| Failure reply names all three ways forward, no `Choices:` line | 20 of 20 |
| …and also says the printer can still prepare prints | 17 of 20 |
| "Skip it for now" says it's ready and Connect… on Home is there for later | 20 of 20 |
| "How long does this take?" answered with 30 seconds | 20 of 20 |

- **Live app runs looked over by hand:** 9 runs with the real model. Of the six live runs on the fresh page build, 3 had the stand-in host answering and 3 had it failing; the final build had 3 more failing runs. The Bambu fake ran in all 9. In every run the question typed during the wait was answered first, and the app's note about the outcome came after it.

**Things you should know**
1. **The wait length in the tool result doesn't reach later turns.** The design assumed the model reads it when asked mid-wait. `AgentHost` sends only message text between turns, so the tool result is gone by then. The prompt now asks the checking line to say "up to 30 seconds", and that carries it into the next turn.
2. **My first prompt edit broke an unrelated step.** It dropped "show me the full printer list" from 85 of 90 runs to 66 of 90, but only with the real 383-printer catalogue and a printer found on the network. Removing the word "themselves" fixed it: 29 of 30.
3. **One place drops a waiting attempt.** `PrinterConversation::start()` drops any attempt left waiting. The panel-close call I first added in `PrinterPanel` was redundant, and the probe proved that, so I removed it.
4. **This conflicts with one line of the tool guide.** `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:268` says to use asynchronous behaviour only when Orca's own operation is asynchronous. Cancel also only drops the result; the HTTP request runs on until it times out. This is what we agreed, but a reviewer may point at that line.
5. **Bambu undo is not done.** A Bambu attempt that fails or is cancelled still leaves the printer linked to the device and selected. The undo is more than a few lines, so it's a separate task chip.
6. **Two things not checked.** I haven't built on Windows; the harness's new `boost/asio` include is placed first for that reason. I haven't run the harness's default mode, since this change only touches printer setup code.

The live runs also showed the known problem where the model invents a Bambu device ID (2 of 6 runs). It isn't made worse: the old prompt connected in 18 of 30 runs and the new one in 23 of 30.

I extended the prompt test runner only in my scratchpad; it's still only on `claude/printer-receipt-card`. Nothing is committed. Say if you want a commit or a PR.
Test the app live and capture the screenshot so that I can take a look.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata:

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool

---
name: render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof
description: Have the app draw its own widgets into a PNG for appearance evidence; behavioural assertions miss visual defects entirely, and screen capture is often unavailable.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

For fork-owned wx controls, split painting from the paint event —
`paint(wxPaintEvent&)` builds the DC and delegates to
`draw(wxDC&, wxGraphicsContext&, wxSize)` — then add `snapshot()` that draws into
a `wxMemoryDC` over a `wxBitmap`. The shell harness writes those PNGs each run
(honour an env var like `JUSPRIN_ARTIFACT_DIR`; the harness deletes its temp data
dir at exit, so artifacts written there vanish before you can look).

Note `wxGraphicsContext::Create` has no generic `wxDC` overload — each caller
must build the context for its own concrete DC and pass it in.

**Why:** on the printer/spool chip slice, 267 green harness checks coexisted with
two real rendering defects, both found only by opening the image: a long-name
snapshot byte-identical to the normal one (the capture helper called `refresh()`
first, which re-read the store and undid the test's label — so the width
assertion compared a value to itself), and an inline detail overrunning the
trailing chevron under width pressure (measured width was correct; the overlap
was a painting error). Screen-control access was denied and `screencapture`
could not see the window, so in-app rendering was the only route.

**How to apply:** assert on raw pixel buffers (`wxImage::GetData` + `memcmp`) —
"light differs from dark", "long name differs from normal" — so a silently
reverted label fails instead of passing. Then still *open the image*; the
assertions prove difference, not correctness. See
[[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]].

content.text:
I ran the connect flow live in the fixed app and sent you seven screenshots. It used the real model and real connection tests against three fake Moonraker printers running on local ports: one that fails after 12 seconds, one that never answers, and one that answers after 3 seconds. The run passed with no failed checks. The pictures are the app's own rendering of the panel, taken by WebKit.

What each picture shows:

1. **`1-card`**: the connect card, asking for the API key.
2. **`2-connecting`**: after Connect, the card reads "Connecting…" with a moving progress bar and a Cancel button. The assistant says "I'm checking it now; that can take up to 30 seconds."
3. **`3-asked-while-waiting`**: "how long does this take?" typed during the wait gets "Usually a few seconds, sometimes up to 30 seconds" while the card is still connecting.
4. **`4-failed`**: the card turns red, "Couldn't reach http://127.0.0.1:…". The app's note follows, then the assistant names the three ways forward in words, with no reply buttons.
5. **`5-cancelled`**: a second address, with Cancel tapped while it waits. The card reads "Cancelled" and the app notes the cancel.
6. **`6-connected`**: a third address. The card reads "Connected" in green, the app notes it verified, and the assistant confirms.
7. **`7-home`**: the printer card on Home, with "Sends files over Wi-Fi". The address was saved only once a test had passed.

Things to look at:

- **The model after Cancel (visible in `6-connected`).** After the cancel note, the person wrote "Try http://127.0.0.1:65441." The model answered "It's still waiting on the connection screen. If you want, I can try again with the new address." It connected only after one more message. So it misread the cancel note "The person cancelled connecting Generic Klipper Printer." as something still in progress. That's a wording or prompt problem to fix, and it's the only rough spot in this run.
- **One run is one sample.** The model's words vary between runs; the measured rates are the ones from the earlier batches.
- **Only the panel and Home are pictured.** The snapshots cover web-page content, not the native header or window frame.

To get these files I added a `--printer-connect-capture <dir>` mode to the shell harness, plus a WebKit snapshot helper in `tests/shell/harness_appearance.mm`. They were needed because macOS blocks screen capture from my shell, and the desktop tool's `save_to_disk` again wrote no files. They're uncommitted in the same worktree; keep them or drop them as you prefer. The screenshots themselves are in my scratchpad folder.

I'll commit in two parts: the fix with its tests, and separately the new screenshot-capture harness mode, so it's easy to drop if you don't want it. First, checking the state of `jusprin-newui` and the main checkout it's checked out in.

In --printer-live, the live model can close the printer panel itself
(printer_setup_finish) before the script is done with that session. The
next scripted message then went through live_send(), which dereferenced
the closed panel's null host, and the harness died with exit code 139
and no HARNESS RESULT line.

live_send() now records a failed check named after the running step
(live_panel_open_for_<step>) and sends nothing. live_settled() already
treats a closed panel as settled, so the run moves on, the next open
starts a fresh session, and every run ends with a result line.

Refuse printer_connect calls that have nothing to connect to

When someone asked to connect a Moonraker or OctoPrint printer before
giving its address, the model sometimes called printer_connect with no
address ({"hostType":"moonraker"} or {"address":""}). The printer
panel's own check refused the call, but a refused call still becomes an
activity, and the panel draws every finished printer_connect activity as
"Connect this printer · Sent". The person saw a claim that something was
sent, and only then was asked for the address.

The registry's decoder now accepts exactly one of two argument sets: a
non-empty deviceId alone (Bambu Lab), or hostType with a non-empty
address (Moonraker or OctoPrint). A call the decoder refuses goes back
to the model as an error and never becomes an activity, so nothing is
drawn. The refusal and the schema descriptions tell the model to ask
for the address instead. The panel's check keeps only what the decoder
cannot know: a deviceId sent for a printer that is not a Bambu Lab one.

Verified live with the shell harness and the real model, typing as a
new user, with every call's arguments recorded through a local proxy:
before the change the false "Sent" block appeared in 2 of 3
conversations; after it, 0 of 4, including 2 where the model made the
same incomplete call and then asked for the address. Giving an address

Keep the app responsive while it tests a printer's network address

Connecting a Moonraker or OctoPrint printer from the printer setup
conversation froze the whole app for as long as the printer took to
answer. OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_host ran Orca's blocking
PrintHost::test on the main thread, and a host that accepts the
connection but never replies holds that call with no upper bound
(Http's DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MAX is 0). Meanwhile the connect card said only
"Sent", nothing typed could land, and a failure ended in a reply with
no way forward. It also saved the address to the printer before
testing it, so Home said "Sends files over Wi-Fi" after a failed test.

Now:
- connect_host tests a copy of the printer's settings on a detached
  thread and returns at once. The thread owns the adapter and a verdict
  slot; the backend reads the verdict on the next connection() call.
  Nothing joins the thread, so closing the panel never waits on a slow
  host. The address and API key are saved only when the test passes.
- Host attempts share the Bambu path's 30-second limit
  (kConnectionWait), so a silent host is reported as failed at 30 s.
- A new printer_connect while one is waiting replaces it instead of
  being refused with connection_in_progress. The card's Cancel
  (printer_action cancel_connection) and the start of a new panel
  session drop a waiting attempt, and whatever the printer answers
  later is never read or saved.
- The conversation keeps each card's attempt state and sends it to the
  page, so the card reads Connecting… (with a progress bar and Cancel),
  then Connected, "Couldn't reach <address>" or Cancelled.
- printer_connect's result tells the model the wait ("gives it up to 30
  seconds"). The app sends only message text between turns, so the
  prompt asks the model to say the wait in its "checking" line, where a
  later question can find it. After a failure the prompt asks for the
  three ways forward in words: try again, enter the details in the
  printer settings, or leave it for now since the printer can prepare
  prints without a connection.

Not changed: a failed or cancelled Bambu Lab attempt still leaves the
printer linked to the device and selected. Undoing that is separate
work.

Verified:
- Shell harness (--printer-setup), unfixed build first: a host holding
  the request for 3 s froze a 100 ms timer for 3032 ms (0 ticks) and
  the failed address was saved. Fixed build: 29 ticks in 3010 ms,
  nothing saved; a silent host fails at 30.0 s while the timer keeps
  ticking; success saves the address; Cancel, a replaced attempt and a
  panel closed mid-test save nothing. The panel-close check was shown to
  fail with PrinterConversation::start()'s drop removed.
- agent_bridge_tests: 252 test cases pass, including new ones for
  connecting, replacing, cancelling, the dropped late answer, and a
  message sent while waiting being answered before the outcome's turn.
- AgentUI vitest: 193 tests pass, including the card's states.
- Live model, prompt-only runs (20 each): the failure reply names all
  three ways forward in 20/20 (17/20 also say the printer can still
  prepare prints); "skip it" 20/20; the wait is given as 30 s 20/20.
  An earlier wording ("enter the details themselves") dropped the
  unrelated "show me the full printer list" step from 85/90 to 66/90
  with the real catalogue in context; the committed wording is 29/30.
- Live app (--printer-live, 9 runs): the question typed while waiting
  was answered first and the outcome's note came after it every time.
EOF

The fix is now on `jusprin-newui` as two commits. `jusprin-newui` hadn't moved since I branched, so it landed as a fast-forward with no merge. The main checkout is on the new tip and clean. Nothing is pushed.

- **`c922876c66` "Keep the app responsive while it tests a printer's network address"** is the fix. It covers the host test in the background, saving the address only after a pass, the card states and Cancel, the prompt changes, and the unit and harness tests. The commit message records the before-and-after numbers.
- **`c013c97942` "Add a harness mode that pictures the printer connect flow"** is the `--printer-connect-capture` screenshot mode. It's separate so you can revert it alone. I built the harness without it to confirm the first commit compiles by itself.

Not included and still open:

- **Bambu undo.** A failed or cancelled Bambu Lab connect still leaves the printer linked and selected. That's in the task chip I created earlier.
- **Cancel wording.** In the screenshot run, the model read the "cancelled" note as a connection still waiting.
